_meta.title: Skeletal-muscle twitch & force-frequency properties (measured) — locked input for the §14 twitch-fusion derivation
_meta.what: LOCKED MEASURED inputs (cited, not tuned) used to DERIVE the saturating force-frequency (twitch-fusion) curve as a DIMENSIONLESS function of nu = f*T, and to VALIDATE its shape against the measured sigmoidal tension-frequency relation. Nothing here is fitted to a target.
_meta.derivation: Sum the cited Fuglevand-Winter-Patla analytical twitch h(tau)=tau*exp(1-tau) at dimensionless rate nu=f*T; the steady-state fusion index FI(nu)=F_min/F_max rises monotonically 0->1 and SATURATES, with NO free parameter. This reproduces the measured low-rate-twitch / high-rate-smooth-tetanus fusion (Rack & Westbury 1969).
_meta.validated_claim: the DIMENSIONLESS fusion curve FI(nu) (monotone rise + saturation, and the well-fused knee at nu*~1.08) is derived from the cited twitch form with no tuning; it reproduces the measured sigmoidal tension-frequency shape.
_meta.open_O: the ABSOLUTE fusion frequency f = nu/T (contraction time T is muscle/species-dependent); the twitch:tetanus AMPLITUDE ratio (~3.9x, representative); and the MEAN-force sigmoid plateau (needs nonlinear calcium summation, not modelled here).
_meta.convention_note: the 'well-fused' fusion criterion FI=0.90 used to report nu* is a STATED CONVENTION (a readable landmark on the monotone curve), NOT a measurement and NOT tuned to hit a target; it is defined in code, not taken from this measured block.
_meta.payload_sha256_note: sha256 over canonical json.dumps(measured, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':')); the module recomputes and checks this on every run (locks the data).

fuglevand_winter_patla1993.cite: Fuglevand AJ, Winter DA, Patla AE (1993) Models of recruitment and rate coding organization in motor-unit pools. J Neurophysiol 70:2470-2488. doi:10.1152/jn.1993.70.6.2470
fuglevand_winter_patla1993.twitch_model: analytical motor-unit twitch (impulse response of a critically-damped 2nd-order system): h(t) = (t/T) * exp(1 - t/T), peak amplitude 1 at t = T, where T is the contraction time. In dimensionless form with tau = t/T it carries NO free parameter.
fuglevand_winter_patla1993.normalization_result: force-frequency / fusion behaviour collapses onto a single curve when firing rate f is expressed as the dimensionless product nu = f*T (rate normalized to the inverse contraction time 1/T); curves for units of different T then coincide.
fuglevand_winter_patla1993.verbatim: the twitch was modelled as the impulse response of a critically damped second-order system; when stimulus rate is normalized to the twitch contraction time the force-frequency curves of different motor units are similar

rack_westbury1969.cite: Rack PMH, Westbury DR (1969) The effects of length and stimulus rate on tension in the isometric cat soleus muscle. J Physiol 204:443-460. doi:10.1113/jphysiol.1969.sp008923
rack_westbury1969.preparation: anaesthetised cat, isometric soleus, controlled stimulus rate
rack_westbury1969.tension_frequency_shape: sigmoidal: tension rises with stimulus rate, with progressive fusion of twitches into a smooth tetanus and a high-rate plateau
rack_westbury1969.verbatim: tension increased with stimulus rate along an S-shaped curve; at low rates individual twitches were visible, fusing into a smooth tetanus at higher rates

twitch_tetanus_ratio.note: representative whole-muscle twitch:tetanus (peak tetanic / peak twitch) force ratio; muscle-, species- and temperature-dependent. Sets the AMPLITUDE of a fully-fused tetanus relative to a single twitch; the precise value is left open [O]. NOT tuned to any target.
twitch_tetanus_ratio.cite: order-of-magnitude consistent with Close RI (1972) Dynamic properties of mammalian skeletal muscles. Physiol Rev 52:129-197 (twitch:tetanus typically ~1:3 to ~1:5 across mammalian muscles)

contraction_time_references.human_soleus_cite: Buchthal F, Schmalbruch H (1970) Contraction times and fibre types in intact human muscle. Acta Physiol Scand 79:435-452. doi:10.1111/j.1748-1716.1970.tb04744.x
contraction_time_references.note: contraction time T is muscle/species/fibre-type dependent (tens to ~150+ ms); it sets the ABSOLUTE rate axis f = nu/T and therefore stays open [O]. Only the dimensionless fusion curve in nu is derived/validated here.

fusion_index_definition.FI: FI = F_min / F_max evaluated over one steady-state period of the summed twitch train; FI = 0 for isolated (unfused) twitches and FI -> 1 for a smooth (fully fused) tetanus
fusion_index_definition.derived_property: under linear twitch summation the MEAN force is unbounded in rate (no plateau); what saturates is the FUSION (disappearance of ripple). The sigmoidal MEAN-force plateau of Rack & Westbury additionally requires nonlinear (calcium) summation, which is NOT modelled here and stays open [O].
